claims.excerpt: Selective Availability: Two Separate GPS Changes
claims.claim: The piece concerns two distinct GPS changes involving Selective Availability: stopping its use in 2000 and specifying its omission from GPS III in 2007.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: In May 2000 the US government stopped using it at President Bill Clinton’s direction to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. In September 2007 the government announced it would procure the future GPS III generation without the feature.
claims.narrative: The story distinguishes two changes to Selective Availability, the feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. In May 2000, the US government stopped using it; in September 2007, it announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without it.
claims.explanation: The headline’s distinction matches the separate 2000 operational change and 2007 procurement announcement described in the source.
claims.materiality: The distinction is central to the piece.
